question: Should durable plugin `allow-always` be accepted as a core plugin API and persistent state contract now, and what stable non-sensitive owner/scope should Skill Workshop use before merge?
rationale: The PR changes when future approval prompts can be suppressed and adds plugin-author-facing API surface, which needs maintainer security/product intent beyond mechanical code repair.

options.title: Fix durable Skill Workshop scope before merge
options.body: Require a stable core/plugin owner, a non-sensitive durable key, current-main rebase preservation, and a second-call reuse proof before this PR leaves draft.

options.title: Split the Skill Workshop opt-in
options.body: Land only the generic API after review and keep built-in Skill Workshop lifecycle approvals on `allow-once`/`deny` until its owner/audit model is ready.

options.title: Pause the durable API direction
options.body: Keep this draft open or close it if maintainers decide persistent plugin approval reuse should wait for a broader approval-evidence design.

recommendation.title: Fix durable Skill Workshop scope before merge
recommendation.body: Require a stable core/plugin owner, a non-sensitive durable key, current-main rebase preservation, and a second-call reuse proof before this PR leaves draft.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main approval and Skill Workshop lifecycle commits make this handle the best available owner for the security/product boundary decision.
